context.title: David's Charge and Solomon's Purge
context.summary: David charges Solomon to keep God's law and dies. Solomon then removes Adonijah, banishes Abiathar, and executes Joab and Shimei, making his kingdom secure.
context.background: Adonijah's request for Abishag, David's young attendant, was more than romance: taking a former king's woman could signal a claim to his throne (compare 2 Samuel 16:21-22). Abiathar's banishment to Anathoth, a priestly town near Jerusalem, fulfills the old word against Eli's house.

customs.note: A Hebrew way of saying 'I am about to die' — the road every person eventually walks.

watchFor: David's charge echoes Moses' instructions for kings: keeping the law brings a secure throne (vv. 2–4).
Each death is tied to an earlier wrong — Joab's killings of Abner and Amasa, Shimei's curse (vv. 5–9, 32, 44).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Joab
people.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

people.name: Abner
people.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

people.name: Ner
people.summary: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.”

people.name: Amasa
people.summary: The son of Abigail, a sister of king David (1 Chr. 2:17; 2 Sam. 17:25).

people.name: Jether
people.summary: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: Barzillai
people.summary: A Gileadite of Rogelim who was distinguished for his loyalty to David. He liberally provided for the king’s followers (2 Sam. 17:27).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: A Benjamite of the house of Saul, who stoned and cursed David when he reached Bahurim in his flight from Jerusalem on the occasion of the rebellion of Absalom (2 Sam. 16:5-13).

people.name: Gera
people.summary: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

people.name: Adonijah
people.summary: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.summary: Daughter of the oath, or of seven, called also Bath-shu’a (1 Chr. 3:5), was the daughter of Eliam (2 Sam. 11:3) or Ammiel (1 Chr. 3:5), and wife of Uriah the Hittite.

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

people.name: Abishag
people.summary: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age.

people.name: Abiathar
people.summary: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17).

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

people.name: Eli
people.summary: Ascent, the high priest when the ark was at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3, 9). He was the first of the line of Ithamar, Aaron’s fourth son (1 Chr. 24:3; comp. 2 Sam. 8:17), who held that office.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Achish
people.summary: The king with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 21:10-15). He is called Abimelech in the superscription of Ps. 34. It was probably this same king to whom David a second time repaired at the head of a band of 600 warriors, and who assigned him Ziklag, whence he carried on war against the surrounding tribes (1 Sam. 27:5-12).

people.name: Maachah
people.summary: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

places.name: Bahurim
places.summary: Young men, a place east of Jerusalem (2 Sam. 3:16; 19:16), on the road to the Jordan valley.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Mahanaim
places.summary: Two camps, a place near the Jabbok, beyond Jordan, where Jacob was met by the “angels of God,” and where he divided his retinue into “two hosts” on his return from Padan-aram (Gen. 32:2).

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Anathoth
places.summary: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat.

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: Generally understood as denoting the Messiah, “the peaceful one,” as the word signifies (Gen. 49:10). The Vulgate Version translates the word, “he who is to be sent,” in allusion to the Messiah; the Revised Version, margin, “till he come to Shiloh;” and the LXX., “until that which is his shall come to Shiloh.”

places.name: Kidron
places.summary: Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives.

places.name: Gath
places.summary: A wine-vat, one of the five royal cities of the Philistines (Josh. 13:3) on which the ark brought calamity (1 Sam. 5:8, 9; 6:17). It was famous also as being the birthplace or residence of Goliath (1 Sam. 17:4).

events.title: Death of David
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 2:10–11. People: David. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Reign of Solomon
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 2:12–11:42. People: Solomon. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
